title: Conditional Probability and Bayes' Theorem
welcome_lead: Update beliefs with evidence using conditional probability and Bayes' theorem.
meta_desc: Maths adventure on conditional probability P(A|B) and Bayes' theorem.
final_note: Bayes flips the conditional - prior to posterior!

concepts.def: P(A|B) = P(A); A unaffected by B.
P(A) = Σ P(A|B_i) P(B_i) over partition.

walkthroughs.body_html:
P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, P(A∩B) = 0.2. Find P(A|B).

P(A|B) = 0.2/0.4 = 0.5. Note A and B are independent here.

Draw two-stage tree: first event A (0.7), then B|A (0.6).

P(A∩B) = 0.7 × 0.6 = 0.42 along that branch.
